query: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi has high saturation magnetization but a low coercive field, and reported single-phase fcc high-entropy alloys derived from it have coercive fields no greater than 100 Oe in the reported magnetic measurements. What single intervention could overcome this coercivity limitation? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted change relative to single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a matched derivative, the relevant compositional, structural, and measurement boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: A controlled thermomechanical treatment—specifically annealing under an applied uniaxial stress (or magnetic field)—will induce a preferential crystallographic texture and residual strain in single‐phase fcc FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloys, thereby enhancing magnetocrystalline anisotropy and increasing the coercive field well beyond 100 Oe while preserving the high saturation magnetization.
generation.material_initial_state: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi (or its high-entropy derivative) exhibiting high saturation magnetization and a coercive field of no more than ~100 Oe.
generation.intervention: Anneal the alloy under a controlled applied uniaxial stress (or alternatively, an external magnetic field) during the thermal treatment to promote texture development.
generation.conditions: The treatment should be performed at a temperature below that which might trigger unwanted phase transformations, under ambient to moderately elevated temperatures, and under stress levels that are sufficient to induce texture without causing mechanical damage. Magnetic measurements (e.g., via a vibrating sample magnetometer or SQUID) should be conducted at room temperature under similar field sweep conditions to literature reports.
generation.structural_mediator: Induced preferential crystallographic texture and associated residual stresses that enhance magnetocrystalline anisotropy.
generation.mechanism: The applied uniaxial stress during annealing leads to directional grain growth and texture formation in the fcc matrix. This in turn results in increased magnetocrystalline anisotropy, which impedes domain wall motion and enhances the coercive field. The intervention is designed to achieve these effects without altering the overall fcc structure or significantly affecting the saturation magnetization.
generation.predicted_outcome: The treated alloy should exhibit a coercive field that is significantly enhanced (i.e., well above 100 Oe) relative to the untreated single-phase fcc state, while maintaining a high saturation magnetization.
generation.baseline: Untreated single-phase fcc FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloys with coercivities ≤ 100 Oe.
generation.boundary: The intervention must preserve the single-phase fcc structure (avoid forming secondary phases) and be performed under conditions similar to standard ambient temperature magnetic measurements. The annealing temperature, duration, and stress magnitude must be carefully optimized to avoid unwanted diffusion or phase transformation.
generation.uncertainty: The precise magnitude of the coercivity increase is uncertain and will depend on the specific annealing parameters and stress magnitude; further optimization may be required to maximize the anisotropy without compromising the high saturation magnetization.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of single-phase fcc FeCoNi (or its high-entropy derivative) samples. Subject one set to the proposed annealing under a controlled uniaxial stress (or applied magnetic field) while keeping the other set as an untreated control. After treatment, perform a series of magnetic measurements (e.g., coercivity and saturation magnetization from hysteresis loops) and microstructural characterization (using XRD and TEM) to assess texture development.
measurements: Magnetic hysteresis loops to determine coercive field (Hc) and saturation magnetization (Ms)
X-ray diffraction to detect preferential crystallographic texture
TEM analysis to observe potential residual strain or nanostructural changes
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the stress-annealed samples do not show a statistically significant increase in coercivity beyond 100 Oe relative to the untreated control, or if the fcc structure is compromised (e.g., formation of secondary phases), then the hypothesis that the stress-assisted annealing enhances coercivity is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: In summary, we have achieved high magnetic anisotropy in rare‐earth‐free high entropy metallic thin films by sputtering and RTA. Robust magnetic order of both fcc FeCoNiMnCu and L10 (FeCoNiMnCu)Pt films has been demonstrated. The FeCoNiMnCu films exhibit a large coercivity increase after RTA, resulting from microstructural changes and strain‐induced anisotropy enhancement which strengthens domain wall pinning. Addition of Pt reduces the symmetry of the cubic fcc lattice to an intermetallic tetragonal L10 phase of (FeCoNiMnCu)Pt. Although the Pt insertion lowers the configurational entropy compared to the equiatomic case, the entropy is still high enough to stabilize an L10 single phase. This intermetallic phase is confirmed to host high magnetocrystalline anisotropy, likely attributed to the lower symmetry of the L10 structure and the strong spin‐orbit coupling provided by the Pt insertion. These findings demonstrate the promise of high‐entropy intermetallic design as a key avenue to search for new high‐entropy magnets beyond the equiatomic composition.

In this work, the FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8Snx (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.10) HEAs were prepared by vacuum arc-melt casting. Effects of Sn content on the phase constitution and magnetic properties were studied. All the samples are composed of FCC and BCC phases, whereas some unknown phases appear with the addition of Sn. The addition of Sn promotes the formation of BCC phase, and it also affects the shape of Cu-rich nanoprecipitates in the BCC matrix. Moreover, the Ms increases greatly while the remanence (Br) decreases with the increasing of x for FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8Snx (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.10) HEAs. The addition of Sn can obviously increase the Curie temperature of the FCC phase. The phase of alloys with a mixture of FCC and BCC will transform from FCC to BCC phase at high temperature, leading to an increase of magnetization. They can be used as new soft magnetic materials at high temperatures.

Recently, the magnetic properties of HEAs with varying composition have been extensively investigated. The CuAl contents had obvious influence on the microstructure and saturation magnetization of FeCoNi(CuAl)x alloy, and the Ms of FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8 alloy increased from 78.9 Am2 kg−1 to 93.1 Am2 kg−1 by annealing at 673 K. Annealing can effectively improve the saturation magnetization of a certain constituent. Zhang et al. have prepared the FeCoNi(SiAl)x HEAs by arc-melting method and found that the electrical resistivity increased and sacrificed the magnetization with adding SiAl content, and the coercivity with a single-phase structure (BCC or FCC) was smaller than that of the two-phase structure (BCC and FCC). Therefore, the alloy components and annealing process have great influence on the magnetic properties of alloys. frame.system: Single‐phase face‐centered cubic (fcc) FeCoNi-based high‐entropy alloys that exhibit high saturation magnetization but inherently low coercive fields (~100 Oe).
frame.goal: Enhance the coercive field well above 100 Oe while retaining high saturation magnetization by inducing additional magnetocrystalline anisotropy via a single compositional intervention.
frame.limitation: The intrinsic fcc structure of these alloys produces very low coercivity, with reported values not exceeding 100 Oe, likely due to low anisotropy and easy domain wall motion.
constraints: Maintain the high saturation magnetization characteristic of FeCoNi-based systems
Keep within the compositional and structural bounds of existing fcc high-entropy alloys
Intervention must be a single, minimal addition that does not introduce a major secondary phase
Measurement protocols should be comparable to those reported in the literature
frame.regime: Standard ambient temperature magnetic measurements (using techniques such as vibrating sample magnetometry) with applied field sweeps typical of prior studies.
prior_attempts: Previous studies using pristine, single-phase fcc FeCoNi and its fcc-derived high-entropy variants have consistently reported coercivities ≤100 Oe
Efforts lacking additional anisotropy enhancements (e.g., without altering symmetry or inducing ordering) have failed to overcome this limitation
